“How strong the viewer curiosity gap is”
Your video is competing against emotion, not other creators.

It happens at the angle level.

Because:

YouTube promotes questions, not information.

2) Retention Graph (“Emotional Pulse”) — VERY important but misunderstood
The board says:
* Dips = lost attention

This is actually one of the most valuable insights on the board.
Here’s what many creators don’t realize:
YouTube does not measure watch time the way creators think.
It measures:
Satisfaction probability
A spike in retention often means:
* confusion
* surprise
* emotional reaction
* new information
A dip often means:
* predictable
* slow explanation
* already understood

Creators think retention is about editing speed.
It’s not.
Retention is about:
Question → Delay → Payoff
If a video answers too quickly → viewers leave.​
If it delays with tension → viewers stay.

1) The Biggest Shift — YouTube Is No Longer Video-Based
From the first board “YouTube’s 2026 Algorithm: 9 Game-Changing Updates”
The most important insight:
YouTube now optimizes for viewer satisfaction, not watch time.
Old model:
Long videos = rewarded
New model:
Why the viewer stopped watching = rewarded or punished
Meaning:
* If they leave because their question was answered → GOOD
* If they leave because bored → BAD
So the goal is NOT:​
“make longer videos”
The real goal is:
Solve a curiosity FAST but keep psychological interest.
This perfectly matches symptom content.
Why your niche works:​
A symptom video answers quickly but creates a bigger personal question:
“Is this happening to me?”

The 7 Viral Title Engines (Very Important)

1) “What It Feels Like”
Trigger: embodied empathy
Examples:
* What getting killed by fentanyl feels like
* What trench warfare felt like
Why it works:​
The brain simulates physical experience.​
Viewer safely experiences danger.
For your channel:​
“what low blood sugar actually feels like”
This is extremely powerful for health.
2) “What It’s Like to Be Every X”
Trigger: forbidden access
Viewer gets insider perspective.
Brain reaction:​
“I am entering a hidden world.”
Health adaptation:​
“What it’s like inside your body during a panic attack”
3) POV: You Are X
Trigger: identity insertion
Viewer becomes the character.
They are not watching anymore.​
They are participating.
Health example:​
“POV: your brain is low on oxygen”
This is gold for Shorts.
4) “Should Not Exist”
Trigger: reality violation
Human brain is hypersensitive to impossible things.
Health adaptation:​
“Symptoms your body should not be doing”
5) “What Happened After…”
Trigger: unfinished story curiosity
Brain hates unresolved outcomes.
Health adaptation:​
“What happens to your body after years of sleep deprivation”
6) “Worst Ever”
Trigger: fear + survival instinct
Fear is the strongest retention emotion.
Health adaptation:​
“The worst dehydration mistake people make”
7) “X Just Did Something Impossible”
Trigger: urgency + novelty
The word “just” activates immediacy.
Health example:​
“Doctors just discovered why people wake at 3am”
